degreeTitle: B.S. in Applied Physiology and Kinesiology — Pre-Physical Therapy Concentration
acuAlignNote: Palm Beach Atlantic University's Applied Physiology and Kinesiology, B.S. — Concentration in Pre-Physical Therapy (120 credit hours, West Palm Beach Campus) is a real, dedicated pre-PT degree, re-checked directly against PBA's own course catalog. Ten required courses map directly: BIO 2281/2283 Human Anatomy and Physiology I (Anatomical Foundations); BIO 1101/1103 and BIO 1111/1113 Biology I & II (general biology content); HHP 3263 Physiology of Exercise (Physiological Bases of Exercise); HHP 4203 Advanced Clinical Physiology (Exercise Physiology: Adaptation); HHP 3013 Clinical Exercise for Special Populations (Exercise Prescription); HHP 3233 Kinesiology (Mechanical Bases of Exercise); HHP 4003 Biomechanics (a direct match for the Biomechanics unit); HHP 3423 Personal Fitness Assessment and Exercise Prescription (Exercise Prescription and Delivery); HHP 3343 Research Methods (research-methods content); and HHP 4433 Field Experience Internship, reinforced by HHP 4813 Senior Research (the required internship/clinical component). Several other relevant courses — HHP 3033 Psychology of Sport, HHP 4303 Topics in Strength and Conditioning, and HHP 4023 Motor Development — exist but are only offered as electives (students choose two of nine listed options), so they are not counted here since they are not guaranteed. WES evaluation required for ACU credit recognition; confirm specific course equivalences with a PBA academic advisor before transfer planning.

That table is labelled 'CA Resident TOTAL' and Cal State LA publishes NO non-resident total — only the statewide surcharge of $471 a unit. The surcharge is annualised here at 26 units ($12,246), which is the basis its sister CSU campus Fullerton publishes for the identical $471 rate (13 units a semester), giving tuition $20,184. A 24-unit floor would be $11,304 (−$942) and a 30-unit load $14,130 (+$1,884), so the plausible band is roughly $40,900–$43,700. kinRank: Exercise Science B.S. with a Pre-Professional concentration built for physical therapy and occupational therapy graduate study
acuAlignNote: Indiana Tech's Exercise Science - Pre-Professional Concentration, B.S. (122 credits, 2026-2027 catalog) is written for students heading to physical therapy, occupational therapy or chiropractic school. Required courses match 9 of the 16 ACU units: Human Anatomy and Physiology I (BIO 2710/2720 or HSC 2010) for EXSC142; Principles of Biology II (BIO 1350/1360) for Human Biology; Exercise Physiology (ES 3730) for EXSC126; Biomechanics (ES 3410) for EXSC321; Fitness Assessment (ES 3740) with Exercise Principles and Programming I (ES 3850) for EXSC233; Human Growth and Development (PSY 1750) for EXSC187; and Motor Learning & Development (ES 3700) for EXSC230. Two more depend on choices within the degree: students pick Sport Psychology (PSY 3530) or Health Psychology, and pick either a two-course research sequence or the pre-internship seminar and internship (ES 4900/4950). This count assumes Sport Psychology and the internship, which are the choices that fit a physical therapy path. There is only one exercise physiology course, no separate functional anatomy or resistance-training course, and no clinical exercise prescription course.

fin.internationalNote: 2026-27 direct billed cost $48,860, from Indiana Tech's Traditional Undergraduate cost sheet: tuition $16,436 per semester for 12-18 credits ($32,872 a year); a double room in Kalbfleisch Hall, which the school tells students to use for estimates, $7,350, plus the full meal plan $5,972 ($13,322); the student services fee $560 plus the $2,106 program fee for Engineering, Computer and Other Sciences ($2,666). The cost sheet does not say whether Exercise Science pays that program fee, so it is included to be safe; without it the total is $46,754. Textbook rental is included in tuition. Student health insurance ($2,486 a year) is left out, as it is for every school in this guide. NAIA teams share 12 scholarship equivalencies with no per-player cap, so a large athletic award is possible, and international merit aid runs from $5,000 to $18,000 a year by high school GPA.

rec: Indiana Tech wins a lot at NAIA level: five straight WHAC Tournament titles (2021-2025) and national quarterfinal runs in 2021, 2023 and 2025. Its Exercise Science Pre-Professional degree is built for physical therapy and occupational therapy school, with internships at local physical therapy and sports performance clinics. The catch is fit with the lifestyle wish list: Fort Wayne is cold in winter and a mid-sized city. The midfield is crowded with junior transfers who will still be there in 2027, so first-year minutes would be a fight. Jack Rose takes charge for his first full season in 2026 after two years as an assistant.
